resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Exception Handling[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

When an exception occurs, the program stops executing.
To handle exceptions, and to call code when an exception occurs, you can use a[b] try/except[/b] statement.
The [b]try[/b] block contains code that might throw an exception. If that exception occurs, the code in the [b]try[/b] block stops being executed, and the code in the [b]except[/b] block is run. If no error occurs, the code in the [b]except[/b] block doesn't run.

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="344"][b]try:[/b]
   num1 = 7
   num2 = 0
   print (num1 / num2)
   print("Done calculation")
[b]except ZeroDivisionError:[/b]
   print("An error occurred")
   print("due to zero division")[/code]
As the code produces a [b]ZeroDivisionError[/b] exception, the code in the except block is run.
[note]In the code above, the [b]except[/b] statement defines the type of exception to handle (in our case, the [b]ZeroDivisionError[/b]).[/note]

[s0l0!-header][h1]Exception Handling[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

A [b]try [/b]statement can have multiple different [b]except [/b]blocks to handle different exceptions.
Multiple exceptions can also be put into a single [b]except [/b]block using parentheses, to have the [b]except [/b]block handle all of them.[code format="py" codeId="345"][b]try:[/b]
   variable = 10
   print(variable + "hello")
   print(variable / 2)
[b]except [/b]ZeroDivisionError:
   print("Divided by zero")
[b]except [/b](ValueError, TypeError):
   print("Error occurred")[/code]
[note]You can handle as many exceptions in the [b]except[/b] statement as you need.[/note]

一个**try**语句可以有多个不同的**except**块来处理不同的异常。
多个异常也可以用圆括号放在一个**except**块中，让**except**块处理所有的异常。

[s0l0!-header][h1]Exception Handling[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

An [b]except[/b] statement without any exception specified will catch all errors. These should be used sparingly, as they can catch unexpected errors and hide programming mistakes.

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="346"][b]try:[/b]
   word = "spam"
   print(word / 0)
[b]except:[/b]
   print("An error occurred")[/code]
[note]Exception handling is particularly useful when dealing with user input.[/note]

resolved.title: ATM取款机
resolved.problem_statement_md:
一台ATM机当用户输入取钱的金额后会自动调用相应的取钱方法`withdraw()`。

如果输入的不是一个数字，机器输出"Please enter a number"。
请使用异常处理将一个数字作为输入，并调用`withdraw()`方法，在输入不是数字的情况下输出 "Please enter a number"。
resolved.problem_statement_en_md:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Exception Handling[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

An ATM machine takes the amount to be withdrawn as input and calls the corresponding withdrawal method.
In case the input is not a number, the machine should output "Please enter a number".
Use exception handling to take a number as input, call the withdraw() method with the input as its argument, and output "Please enter a number", in case the input is not a number.
[note]A [b]ValueError[/b] is raised when you try to convert a non-integer to an integer using [b]int[/b]().[/note]
resolved.hint_md: 当你试图使用`int()`将一个非整数转换为整数时，会产生一个**ValueError**。
